request.user:
[2021 summer phd applied — problem 1]

Problem 1 (Semi-supervised logistic regression). $(X_i, Y_i)$ i.i.d. with $Y \sim \mathrm{Bern}(\tfrac12)$; $X \mid Y=0 \sim N((-6,-6), \mathrm{diag}(5^2, 15^2))$ and $X \mid Y=1 \sim N((6,6), \mathrm{diag}(5^2, 10^2))$. Observe labeled $S_\ell = \{(X_i, Y_i)\}_{i\le n_1}$ and unlabeled $S_u = \{X_i\}_{i>n_1}$. Fit logistic model $P(Y=1\mid x) = \frac{e^{\beta_0 + \beta^T x}}{1 + e^{\beta_0+\beta^T x}}$; $(\hat\beta_0, \hat\beta)$ is the MLE on labeled data, and $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ solves $0 = \frac{1}{n_1}\sum_{i\le n_1} Y_i(1, X_i^T)^T - \frac1n\sum_{i\le n}\pi(X_i;\beta_0,\beta)(1, X_i^T)^T$ (using unlabeled data). Use the given R data-generation code (set.seed(1)).
1) Explain why the logistic model is misspecified in this setting.
2) Report $(\hat\beta_0, \hat\beta)$ on training data and the average test log-likelihood and classification accuracy.
3) Find a loss $L(\beta_0, \beta)$ such that $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ minimizes it.
4) Write an R function computing $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ via Newton-Raphson.
5) Report $(\tilde\beta_0, \tilde\beta)$ and its average test log-likelihood and classification accuracy.
6) Plot the training data (labeled + unlabeled) with the three classification lines (from $\hat\beta$, $\tilde\beta$, and the MLE using all $xs, ys$).

Let  
\[
\theta=(\beta_0,\beta_1,\beta_2)^T,\qquad z(x)=(1,x_1,x_2)^T,\qquad 
\pi_\theta(x)=\frac{\exp(\theta^Tz(x))}{1+\exp(\theta^Tz(x))}.
\]

A caveat: the prompt as pasted does **not** include the actual R code giving \(n_1,n\), the test sample size, or the exact object names. Thus the exact numerical values in Parts 2 and 5 are not uniquely determined from the text alone. I give below the exact R code that reports them once the given `set.seed(1)` data-generation code has been run.

---

## 1) Why the logistic model is misspecified

Because \(Y\sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), the true conditional log-odds are

\[
\log \frac{P(Y=1\mid X=x)}{P(Y=0\mid X=x)}
=
\log \frac{f_1(x)}{f_0(x)},
\]

where \(f_y\) is the density of \(X\mid Y=y\). Here

\[
X\mid Y=0\sim N\left((-6,-6),\begin{pmatrix}25&0\\0&225\end{pmatrix}\right),
\]

\[
X\mid Y=1\sim N\left((6,6),\begin{pmatrix}25&0\\0&100\end{pmatrix}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
\log \frac{f_1(x)}{f_0(x)}
=
-\frac12\log\frac{|\Sigma_1|}{|\Sigma_0|}
-\frac12\left\{(x-\mu_1)^T\Sigma_1^{-1}(x-\mu_1)
-(x-\mu_0)^T\Sigma_0^{-1}(x-\mu_0)\right\}.
\]

Since

\[
|\Sigma_1|=25\cdot 100=2500,\qquad |\Sigma_0|=25\cdot 225=5625,
\]

we get

\[
-\frac12\log\frac{|\Sigma_1|}{|\Sigma_0|}
=
-\frac12\log\frac{4}{9}
=
\log\frac32.
\]

Expanding coordinatewise gives

\[
\log \frac{P(Y=1\mid X=x)}{P(Y=0\mid X=x)}
=
\log\frac32 -0.1 + \frac{12}{25}x_1+\frac{13}{150}x_2-\frac{1}{360}x_2^2.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
\operatorname{logit}\{P(Y=1\mid X=x)\}
=
0.305465\ldots+0.48x_1+0.086667x_2-0.002778x_2^2.
\]

This is **quadratic** in \(x_2\), not linear in \(x\). Therefore the working logistic model

\[
\operatorname{logit}\{P(Y=1\mid X=x)\}=\beta_0+\beta_1x_1+\beta_2x_2
\]

is misspecified.

---

## 2) Labeled-data logistic MLE and test performance

Let the training data objects from the given R code be called `xs`, `ys`, with `xs` an \(n\times 2\) matrix and `ys` a \(0/1\) vector. Let the test data be called `xs.test`, `ys.test`. Rename these below if the original code used different names.

The labeled-data MLE is obtained by fitting logistic regression only on observations \(1,\dots,n_1\).

```r
log1pexp_stable <- function(a) {
  out <- numeric(length(a))
  idx <- a > 0
  out[idx] <- a[idx] + log1p(exp(-a[idx]))
  out[!idx] <- log1p(exp(a[!idx]))
  out
}

eval_theta <- function(theta, x, y) {
  X <- cbind(1, as.matrix(x))
  eta <- drop(X %*% theta)
  avg_loglik <- mean(y * eta - log1pexp_stable(eta))
  acc <- mean((eta >= 0) == (y == 1))
  c(avg_test_loglik = avg_loglik, test_accuracy = acc)
}

## labeled-data logistic regression
dat.labeled <- data.frame(
  y = ys[1:n1],
  x1 = xs[1:n1, 1],
  x2 = xs[1:n1, 2]
)

fit.hat <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = dat.labeled, family = binomial())

theta.hat <- unname(coef(fit.hat))
names(theta.hat) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")

perf.hat <- eval_theta(theta.hat, xs.test, ys.test)

report.hat <- c(theta.hat, perf.hat)
print(report.hat)
```

This prints

\[
(\hat\beta_0,\hat\beta_1,\hat\beta_2),
\]

the average test log-likelihood, and the test classification accuracy.

The average test log-likelihood being computed is

\[
\frac1{N_{\text{test}}}\sum_{j=1}^{N_{\text{test}}}
\left[
Y_j^{\text{test}}\theta^T z(X_j^{\text{test}})
-\log\{1+\exp(\theta^T z(X_j^{\text{test}}))\}
\right].
\]

The classifier is

\[
\widehat Y(x)=1\{\hat\theta^Tz(x)\ge 0\}.
\]

---

## 3) Loss minimized by \((\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta)\)

Define

\[
\bar m_\ell
=
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z(X_i).
\]

Consider the loss

\[
L(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \log\left\{1+\exp(\theta^Tz(X_i))\right\}
-
\theta^T\bar m_\ell.
\]

Then

\[
\nabla_\theta L(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \pi_\theta(X_i)z(X_i)
-
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z(X_i).
\]

Therefore the first-order condition

\[
\nabla_\theta L(\theta)=0
\]

is exactly

\[
0
=
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z(X_i)
-
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_\theta(X_i)z(X_i),
\]

which is the estimating equation defining \(\tilde\theta=(\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta_1,\tilde\beta_2)^T\).

Moreover,

\[
\nabla_\theta^2 L(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\pi_\theta(X_i)\{1-\pi_\theta(X_i)\}z(X_i)z(X_i)^T,
\]

which is positive semidefinite. Hence \(L\) is convex. By the first-order optimality theorem for differentiable convex functions, any solution of the estimating equation is a global minimizer of \(L\). If the design points span \(\mathbb R^3\), the Hessian is positive definite and the minimizer is unique.

---

## 4) Newton-Raphson function for \(\tilde\theta\)

Newton-Raphson uses

\[
g(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \pi_\theta(X_i)z(X_i)-\bar m_\ell,
\]

and

\[
H(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\pi_\theta(X_i)\{1-\pi_\theta(X_i)\}z(X_i)z(X_i)^T.
\]

The Newton update is

\[
\theta^{(k+1)}
=
\theta^{(k)}-H(\theta^{(k)})^{-1}g(\theta^{(k)}).
\]

Here is an R implementation.

```r
ssl_logit_nr <- function(xs, ys, n1, start = NULL,
                         tol = 1e-10, maxit = 100,
                         trace = FALSE, line.search = TRUE) {
  X <- cbind(1, as.matrix(xs))
  n <- nrow(X)
  p <- ncol(X)
  
  if (is.null(start)) {
    start <- rep(0, p)
  }
  
  theta <- as.numeric(start)
  
  ## labeled response moment
  X.l <- X[1:n1, , drop = FALSE]
  y.l <- ys[1:n1]
  m.l <- drop(crossprod(X.l, y.l)) / n1
  
  log1pexp_stable <- function(a) {
    out <- numeric(length(a))
    idx <- a > 0
    out[idx] <- a[idx] + log1p(exp(-a[idx]))
    out[!idx] <- log1p(exp(a[!idx]))
    out
  }
  
  obj <- function(theta) {
    eta <- drop(X %*% theta)
    mean(log1pexp_stable(eta)) - sum(theta * m.l)
  }
  
  converged <- FALSE
  
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    eta <- drop(X %*% theta)
    prob <- plogis(eta)
    
    g <- drop(crossprod(X, prob)) / n - m.l
    W <- prob * (1 - prob)
    H <- crossprod(X, X * W) / n
    
    if (max(abs(g)) < tol) {
      converged <- TRUE
      break
    }
    
    step <- as.numeric(solve(H, g))
    
    theta.old <- theta
    obj.old <- obj(theta.old)
    
    if (line.search) {
      alpha <- 1
      gd <- sum(g * step)
      
      repeat {
        theta.new <- theta.old - alpha * step
        obj.new <- obj(theta.new)
        
        if (obj.new <= obj.old - 1e-4 * alpha * gd || alpha < 1e-8) {
          break
        }
        
        alpha <- alpha / 2
      }
    } else {
      alpha <- 1
      theta.new <- theta.old - step
      obj.new <- obj(theta.new)
    }
    
    if (trace) {
      cat("iter =", it,
          "obj =", obj.new,
          "max|grad| =", max(abs(g)),
          "alpha =", alpha, "\n")
    }
    
    theta <- theta.new
    
    if (max(abs(theta - theta.old)) < tol * (1 + max(abs(theta.old)))) {
      converged <- TRUE
      break
    }
  }
  
  names(theta) <- c("beta0", paste0("beta", seq_len(p - 1)))
  
  list(
    coefficients = theta,
    objective = obj(theta),
    gradient = g,
    iterations = it,
    converged = converged
  )
}
```

---

## 5) Semi-supervised estimator and test performance

Using the labeled-data MLE as a starting point:

```r
fit.ssl <- ssl_logit_nr(xs, ys, n1, start = theta.hat, trace = TRUE)

theta.tilde <- fit.ssl$coefficients
perf.tilde <- eval_theta(theta.tilde, xs.test, ys.test)

report.tilde <- c(theta.tilde, perf.tilde)
print(report.tilde)
```

This prints

\[
(\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta_1,\tilde\beta_2),
\]

the average test log-likelihood, and the test classification accuracy.

The semi-supervised estimator differs from the labeled MLE because it uses the empirical distribution of all covariates \(X_1,\dots,X_n\) in the model-implied moment

\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \pi_\theta(X_i)z(X_i),
\]

while using only labeled observations in

\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z(X_i).
\]

---

## 6) Plot with three classification lines

The three classification boundaries are of the form

\[
\theta^Tz(x)=0,
\]

i.e.

\[
\beta_0+\beta_1x_1+\beta_2x_2=0.
\]

If \(\beta_2\neq 0\), then the line plotted with \(x_1\) on the horizontal axis and \(x_2\) on the vertical axis is

\[
x_2=-\frac{\beta_0}{\beta_2}-\frac{\beta_1}{\beta_2}x_1.
\]

First compute the MLE using all labels, only for comparison:

```r
dat.all <- data.frame(
  y = ys,
  x1 = xs[, 1],
  x2 = xs[, 2]
)

fit.all <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = dat.all, family = binomial())

theta.all <- unname(coef(fit.all))
names(theta.all) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")
```

Then plot:

```r
add_class_line <- function(theta, col, lty, lwd = 2) {
  if (abs(theta[3]) > 1e-12) {
    abline(a = -theta[1] / theta[3],
           b = -theta[2] / theta[3],
           col = col, lty = lty, lwd = lwd)
  } else {
    abline(v = -theta[1] / theta[2],
           col = col, lty = lty, lwd = lwd)
  }
}

n <- nrow(xs)
labeled.idx <- seq_len(n1)
unlabeled.idx <- setdiff(seq_len(n), labeled.idx)

plot(xs[, 1], xs[, 2],
     type = "n",
     xlab = expression(X[1]),
     ylab = expression(X[2]),
     main = "Training data and classification lines")

## Unlabeled points
points(xs[unlabeled.idx, 1],
       xs[unlabeled.idx, 2],
       pch = 16,
       col = "gray75")

## Labeled points, colored by observed class
points(xs[labeled.idx, 1],
       xs[labeled.idx, 2],
       pch = ifelse(ys[labeled.idx] == 1, 19, 1),
       col = ifelse(ys[labeled.idx] == 1, "firebrick", "navy"))

## Add classification lines
add_class_line(theta.hat,   col = "black",     lty = 1)
add_class_line(theta.tilde, col = "darkgreen", lty = 2)
add_class_line(theta.all,   col = "orange",    lty = 3)

legend("topleft",
       legend = c("unlabeled X",
                  "labeled Y=0",
                  "labeled Y=1",
                  "labeled MLE",
                  "semi-supervised",
                  "all-label MLE"),
       col = c("gray75", "navy", "firebrick",
               "black", "darkgreen", "orange"),
       pch = c(16, 1, 19, NA, NA, NA),
       lty = c(NA, NA, NA, 1, 2, 3),
       lwd = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, 2, 2),
       bty = "n")
```

The black line is the labeled-data logistic MLE, the dark green dashed line is the semi-supervised estimator, and the orange dotted line is the logistic MLE using all labels.

## 2) Labeled-data logistic MLE and test performance

Let the training data objects from the given R code be called `xs`, `ys`, with `xs` an \(n\times 2\) matrix and `ys` a \(0/1\) vector. Let the test data be called `xs.test`, `ys.test`. Rename these below if the original code used different names.

The labeled-data MLE is obtained by fitting logistic regression only on observations \(1,\dots,n_1\).

```r
log1pexp_stable <- function(a) {
  out <- numeric(length(a))
  idx <- a > 0
  out[idx] <- a[idx] + log1p(exp(-a[idx]))
  out[!idx] <- log1p(exp(a[!idx]))
  out
}

eval_theta <- function(theta, x, y) {
  X <- cbind(1, as.matrix(x))
  eta <- drop(X %*% theta)
  avg_loglik <- mean(y * eta - log1pexp_stable(eta))
  acc <- mean((eta >= 0) == (y == 1))
  c(avg_test_loglik = avg_loglik, test_accuracy = acc)
}

## labeled-data logistic regression
dat.labeled <- data.frame(
  y = ys[1:n1],
  x1 = xs[1:n1, 1],
  x2 = xs[1:n1, 2]
)

fit.hat <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = dat.labeled, family = binomial())

theta.hat <- unname(coef(fit.hat))
names(theta.hat) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")

perf.hat <- eval_theta(theta.hat, xs.test, ys.test)

report.hat <- c(theta.hat, perf.hat)
print(report.hat)
```

This prints

\[
(\hat\beta_0,\hat\beta_1,\hat\beta_2),
\]

the average test log-likelihood, and the test classification accuracy.

The average test log-likelihood being computed is

\[
\frac1{N_{\text{test}}}\sum_{j=1}^{N_{\text{test}}}
\left[
Y_j^{\text{test}}\theta^T z(X_j^{\text{test}})
-\log\{1+\exp(\theta^T z(X_j^{\text{test}}))\}
\right].
\]

The classifier is

\[
\widehat Y(x)=1\{\hat\theta^Tz(x)\ge 0\}.
\]

---

## 3) Loss minimized by \((\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta)\)

Define

\[
\bar m_\ell
=
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z(X_i).
\]

Consider the loss

\[
L(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \log\left\{1+\exp(\theta^Tz(X_i))\right\}
-
\theta^T\bar m_\ell.
\]

Then

\[
\nabla_\theta L(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \pi_\theta(X_i)z(X_i)
-
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z(X_i).
\]

Therefore the first-order condition

\[
\nabla_\theta L(\theta)=0
\]

is exactly

\[
0
=
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z(X_i)
-
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\pi_\theta(X_i)z(X_i),
\]

which is the estimating equation defining \(\tilde\theta=(\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta_1,\tilde\beta_2)^T\).

Moreover,

\[
\nabla_\theta^2 L(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\pi_\theta(X_i)\{1-\pi_\theta(X_i)\}z(X_i)z(X_i)^T,
\]

which is positive semidefinite. Hence \(L\) is convex. By the first-order optimality theorem for differentiable convex functions, any solution of the estimating equation is a global minimizer of \(L\). If the design points span \(\mathbb R^3\), the Hessian is positive definite and the minimizer is unique.

---

## 4) Newton-Raphson function for \(\tilde\theta\)

Newton-Raphson uses

\[
g(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \pi_\theta(X_i)z(X_i)-\bar m_\ell,
\]

and

\[
H(\theta)
=
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n
\pi_\theta(X_i)\{1-\pi_\theta(X_i)\}z(X_i)z(X_i)^T.
\]

The Newton update is

\[
\theta^{(k+1)}
=
\theta^{(k)}-H(\theta^{(k)})^{-1}g(\theta^{(k)}).
\]

Here is an R implementation.

```r
ssl_logit_nr <- function(xs, ys, n1, start = NULL,
                         tol = 1e-10, maxit = 100,
                         trace = FALSE, line.search = TRUE) {
  X <- cbind(1, as.matrix(xs))
  n <- nrow(X)
  p <- ncol(X)
  
  if (is.null(start)) {
    start <- rep(0, p)
  }
  
  theta <- as.numeric(start)
  
  ## labeled response moment
  X.l <- X[1:n1, , drop = FALSE]
  y.l <- ys[1:n1]
  m.l <- drop(crossprod(X.l, y.l)) / n1
  
  log1pexp_stable <- function(a) {
    out <- numeric(length(a))
    idx <- a > 0
    out[idx] <- a[idx] + log1p(exp(-a[idx]))
    out[!idx] <- log1p(exp(a[!idx]))
    out
  }
  
  obj <- function(theta) {
    eta <- drop(X %*% theta)
    mean(log1pexp_stable(eta)) - sum(theta * m.l)
  }
  
  converged <- FALSE
  
  for (it in seq_len(maxit)) {
    eta <- drop(X %*% theta)
    prob <- plogis(eta)
    
    g <- drop(crossprod(X, prob)) / n - m.l
    W <- prob * (1 - prob)
    H <- crossprod(X, X * W) / n
    
    if (max(abs(g)) < tol) {
      converged <- TRUE
      break
    }
    
    step <- as.numeric(solve(H, g))
    
    theta.old <- theta
    obj.old <- obj(theta.old)
    
    if (line.search) {
      alpha <- 1
      gd <- sum(g * step)
      
      repeat {
        theta.new <- theta.old - alpha * step
        obj.new <- obj(theta.new)
        
        if (obj.new <= obj.old - 1e-4 * alpha * gd || alpha < 1e-8) {
          break
        }
        
        alpha <- alpha / 2
      }
    } else {
      alpha <- 1
      theta.new <- theta.old - step
      obj.new <- obj(theta.new)
    }
    
    if (trace) {
      cat("iter =", it,
          "obj =", obj.new,
          "max|grad| =", max(abs(g)),
          "alpha =", alpha, "\n")
    }
    
    theta <- theta.new
    
    if (max(abs(theta - theta.old)) < tol * (1 + max(abs(theta.old)))) {
      converged <- TRUE
      break
    }
  }
  
  names(theta) <- c("beta0", paste0("beta", seq_len(p - 1)))
  
  list(
    coefficients = theta,
    objective = obj(theta),
    gradient = g,
    iterations = it,
    converged = converged
  )
}
```

## 5) Semi-supervised estimator and test performance

Using the labeled-data MLE as a starting point:

```r
fit.ssl <- ssl_logit_nr(xs, ys, n1, start = theta.hat, trace = TRUE)

theta.tilde <- fit.ssl$coefficients
perf.tilde <- eval_theta(theta.tilde, xs.test, ys.test)

report.tilde <- c(theta.tilde, perf.tilde)
print(report.tilde)
```

This prints

\[
(\tilde\beta_0,\tilde\beta_1,\tilde\beta_2),
\]

the average test log-likelihood, and the test classification accuracy.

The semi-supervised estimator differs from the labeled MLE because it uses the empirical distribution of all covariates \(X_1,\dots,X_n\) in the model-implied moment

\[
\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \pi_\theta(X_i)z(X_i),
\]

while using only labeled observations in

\[
\frac1{n_1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}Y_i z(X_i).
\]

## 6) Plot with three classification lines

The three classification boundaries are of the form

\[
\theta^Tz(x)=0,
\]

i.e.

\[
\beta_0+\beta_1x_1+\beta_2x_2=0.
\]

If \(\beta_2\neq 0\), then the line plotted with \(x_1\) on the horizontal axis and \(x_2\) on the vertical axis is

\[
x_2=-\frac{\beta_0}{\beta_2}-\frac{\beta_1}{\beta_2}x_1.
\]

First compute the MLE using all labels, only for comparison:

```r
dat.all <- data.frame(
  y = ys,
  x1 = xs[, 1],
  x2 = xs[, 2]
)

fit.all <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = dat.all, family = binomial())

theta.all <- unname(coef(fit.all))
names(theta.all) <- c("beta0", "beta1", "beta2")
```

Then plot:

```r
add_class_line <- function(theta, col, lty, lwd = 2) {
  if (abs(theta[3]) > 1e-12) {
    abline(a = -theta[1] / theta[3],
           b = -theta[2] / theta[3],
           col = col, lty = lty, lwd = lwd)
  } else {
    abline(v = -theta[1] / theta[2],
           col = col, lty = lty, lwd = lwd)
  }
}

n <- nrow(xs)
labeled.idx <- seq_len(n1)
unlabeled.idx <- setdiff(seq_len(n), labeled.idx)

plot(xs[, 1], xs[, 2],
     type = "n",
     xlab = expression(X[1]),
     ylab = expression(X[2]),
     main = "Training data and classification lines")

## Unlabeled points
points(xs[unlabeled.idx, 1],
       xs[unlabeled.idx, 2],
       pch = 16,
       col = "gray75")

## Labeled points, colored by observed class
points(xs[labeled.idx, 1],
       xs[labeled.idx, 2],
       pch = ifelse(ys[labeled.idx] == 1, 19, 1),
       col = ifelse(ys[labeled.idx] == 1, "firebrick", "navy"))

## Add classification lines
add_class_line(theta.hat,   col = "black",     lty = 1)
add_class_line(theta.tilde, col = "darkgreen", lty = 2)
add_class_line(theta.all,   col = "orange",    lty = 3)

legend("topleft",
       legend = c("unlabeled X",
                  "labeled Y=0",
                  "labeled Y=1",
                  "labeled MLE",
                  "semi-supervised",
                  "all-label MLE"),
       col = c("gray75", "navy", "firebrick",
               "black", "darkgreen", "orange"),
       pch = c(16, 1, 19, NA, NA, NA),
       lty = c(NA, NA, NA, 1, 2, 3),
       lwd = c(NA, NA, NA, 2, 2, 2),
       bty = "n")
```

The black line is the labeled-data logistic MLE, the dark green dashed line is the semi-supervised estimator, and the orange dotted line is the logistic MLE using all labels.
